events.title: Swift programming language announced at WWDC
events.summary: Apple announced Swift at WWDC on June 2, 2014 — a modern replacement for Objective-C on iOS and macOS.
events.about: Swift is Apple's language for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro apps — safe optionals, value types, protocols, and async/await. It compiles to native code via LLVM and interoperates with Objective-C and C. Most new App Store apps today are Swift or SwiftUI.

narrative.whyChosen: Swift replaced Objective-C as the default for Apple platform development within a few years.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought memory safety and modern syntax to a massive mobile ecosystem without a new runtime.
narrative.problemSolved: Objective-C's manual retain/release and dated syntax slowed iOS development; Apple needed a safer modern language.

events.title: Crystal 0.1.0 released
events.summary: Ary Borenszweig and Juan Wajnerman released Crystal 0.1.0 on June 19, 2014 — a compiled language with Ruby-like syntax and static typing.
events.about: Crystal compiles to efficient native code via LLVM while keeping Ruby's readable syntax — macros, blocks, and `puts` feel familiar but types are checked at compile time. Used for web backends (Lucky, Amber) and CLI tools where Ruby's MRI speed is too slow.

narrative.whyChosen: Crystal 0.1.0 was the first packaged release promising Ruby ergonomics with C-like performance.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed a gradual path from dynamic Ruby to statically typed native compilation without a new syntax.
narrative.problemSolved: Ruby developers wanted MRI's productivity with compiled speed and type safety for production services.

events.title: Kubernetes open-sourced
events.summary: Google open-sourced Kubernetes on June 10, 2014 at DockerCon — a container orchestrator for deploying and scaling Docker workloads across clusters.
events.about: Kubernetes schedules containers onto nodes, restarts failed pods, rolls out deployments, and exposes services with load balancers. It runs on every major cloud (GKE, EKS, AKS) and on-prem. Example: `kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml` to run three replicas of an API behind an ingress controller.

narrative.whyChosen: Kubernetes won the container orchestration wars and became the operating system of the cloud.
narrative.whyImportant: It standardized how teams run microservices at scale after Docker made containers ubiquitous.
narrative.problemSolved: Running dozens of containers manually on fleets of VMs did not scale; Google open-sourced Borg's lessons for everyone.

events.title: Ian Goodfellow invents GANs
events.summary: Ian Goodfellow proposed Generative Adversarial Networks in June 2014 — two-network training that revolutionized synthetic media.
events.about: GANs enabled photorealistic face generation, style transfer, and data augmentation — spawning StyleGAN, deepfakes discourse, and generative model research that preceded diffusion models.

narrative.whyChosen: GANs opened practical generative modeling for images and beyond.
narrative.whyImportant: They introduced adversarial training as a core ML technique.
narrative.problemSolved: Generative models struggled to produce sharp, realistic high-dimensional outputs.
